371207.title: Day–Johnson nonexistence conjecture for equilibria in hypercube Voronoi games
371207.notes: Day-Johnson conjecture (no k-player equilibria on Q_n for large n, every k >= 5). NEW evidence it is FALSE for k = 8: placing the 8 players at all points of a 3-dimensional linear subspace of F_2^n gives an equilibrium for every n from 3 to 22 (exhaustive over GL(3,2)-orbits of subspace profiles for n <= 15: 159 of 485 orbits are equilibria at n=15; explicit near-uniform examples n=16..22, e.g. multiplicities (4,3,3,3,3,3,3) at n=22). Independent brute force (every player, deviation, voter) confirms n=9,10,12. Equilibria appear to require near-uniform multiplicities with odd-part XOR psi != 0. This is numerical evidence only: refuting the conjecture needs an infinite family proved for all n (an analytic, CLT-scale argument with tie/parity effects); no such proof exists yet, and Lean cost is high. Prior art: Stylianou arXiv:2510.25392 (Oct 2025) says open for every k >= 5; web search 2026-11-03 found no later work; not in OpenAI/math 4eaee875 or Omega 86172888. Day-Johnson manuscript is unpublished/unread, so whether they knew subspace profiles is unknown. See claude/voronoi-k8-subspace.json.
